defaultTarget.description: fallback repo for teams that declare none; empty = a team with no repoOwner/repoName gets no env target and relies entirely on the work item's resolved target

perRunBudget.//: Per-run key ceiling for a team with no plan. Optional; falls back to budget, which for a PLANNED team is the Shift pool and not a per-run figure.

plan.description: ordered Rounds of a Shift (run-multi-agent-shifts): each round a reader fan-out or one writer. A team with a plan runs multi-role; without one, dispatch is unchanged. budget doubles as the Shift pool.

maxFixRounds.description: ADR-0017: how many times a reviewer request_changes may re-open the writing Round of this plan. 0 = loop off, the plan runs to exhaustion.

items.//: repoOwner/repoName are NOT required: the repository belongs to the work item, resolved at ingest (R11). They remain as a per-team fallback while teams migrate.

forge.description: Which forge the workers act against; selects the sibling block of the same name. Also the default dialect for a Work Item whose target names no forge (ADR-0023). One active forge per release: a worker pod holds one forge URL and one credential.

url.description: Base URL, no /api/v4. Empty = ploegd configures no GitLab provider, so findings never reach a merge request.

tokenSecret.description: Token with api scope on the target projects, sent as PRIVATE-TOKEN. ADR-0013 tier 2 does not apply on GitLab: per-run push credentials are minted through a Forgejo admin endpoint with no GitLab equivalent, so this shared token is what writing Runs use.

readTokenSecret.description: ADR-0013 tier 1, as for forgejo: a read-only credential for reading Roles, so the reader/writer split is enforced at the forge and not only by scheduling. On GitLab a second project access token at read_repository scope. Empty = readers fall back to the read-write token.

webhookSecret.description: Shared secret GitLab sends as X-Gitlab-Token to POST /webhooks/forge/gitlab. Unset = forge webhooks are rejected, so a human review opens no fix Round and the review loop stays open.

readTokenSecret.description: ADR-0013 tier 1: read-only credential for reading Roles. Empty = readers fall back to the read-write builder token and scheduling is the only boundary (a known gap, closed by creating the secret).

adminTokenSecret.description: ADR-0013 tier 2: credential ploegd uses to MINT per-run push tokens. Held only by ploegd, never by a worker. Unset = nothing is minted.

botUser.description: the forge user whose tokens are minted (default agent-builder)

serviceAccount.description: Worker pods ServiceAccount. create and name are independent: naming an account never suppresses creating it.

config.description: ploegd's routing and roster as a file (mounted at /etc/ploeg/ploeg.yaml). Projects are NAMED and resolved to tracker ids at boot, so no magic numbers live in cluster config. Empty = the legacy PLOEG_TARGET_MAP/PLOEG_TEAM_MAP/PLOEG_TEAM_PLANS env vars still apply.

workerResources.description: Overrides executor.workerResources for this role's workload. Readers do not build, so a fan-out round need not book writer-sized pods.

dindResources.description: Overrides executor.dindResources for this role's DinD sidecar (only rendered when the role runs harness.dind).

planRole.//: name becomes the workload suffix (ploeg-worker-<team>-<role>); writes marks the round's single writer (ADR-0010); cap bounds one Run's spend against the pool (ADR-0012); model/maxReplicaCount/harness override the team's values for this role's workload.
